SAO PAULO, Nov 24 : When a tiny blue chick finally broke free from its shell after weeks of anxious waiting, keepers at Brazil's Sao Paulo Zoo saw more than the birth of a bird; they saw a glimmer of hope for a species that has vanished from the wild.
Aptly named Hope, the female Spix's macaw born in October forms part of a breeding program aimed at rebuilding populations of one of the world's rarest parrots.
Known in Brazil as the Ararinha-azul, the species became internationally famous after inspiring Blu, the main character of the 2011 animated film Rio, a domesticated Spix's macaw who embarks on a journey to save his species.
"We chose 'Hope' because we hope we can give a better future to this species," said Fernanda Guida, head biologist at the zoo's bird division.

Hope's arrival followed a tense 28-day artificial incubation process. Zoo specialists removed the egg for monitoring and eventually intervened when the bird struggled to hatch. Brazil's environment ministry backs the zoo's program.
"It was 28 days of suffering until we saw her hatch. She needed help, we had to remove her from inside the egg because she was badly positioned, and then she hatched," Guida said.
Native to the Caatinga region of northeastern Brazil, Spix's macaws were pushed to the brink of extinction by deforestation and decades of trapping for the illegal pet trade.
The species is classified as "extinct in the wild" by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List, meaning its survival has depended on captive populations.
"That first hatching was a very important milestone for the conservation of the Spix's macaw," Guida said. "It's a long road ahead of us, but it's the path we hope will be very successful."

Source: Reuters

items.title: RFK Jr. Calendars Show Meetings With Lilly, Chipotle CEOs
items.author: list.metadata.agency
items.summary: The US Department of Health and Human Services launched a website hosting more than 92,000 documents including Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s calendars and agency correspondence during the Covid-19 pandemic, in what HHS called a push for greater transparency.
items.body: (Bloomberg) -- The US Department of Health and Human Services launched a website hosting more than 92,000 documents including Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s calendars and agency correspondence during the Covid-19 pandemic, in what HHS called a push for greater transparency.The documents span agencies across the health department and include records previously released under the Freedom of Information Act and other public documents, HHS said in a news release. The department will update the site as more documents are made public.About a quarter of the documents on the new site have not been previously made public, a spokesperson for HHS said.Though Kennedy has been a frequent and vocal critic of corporate influence in medicine and agriculture, his calendars show many meetings with business leaders in healthcare, food and other industries.The calendars list a meeting with Eli Lilly & Co. Chief Executive Dave Ricks in April 2025, a pull-aside during a visit to Indiana when he also met with Governor Mike Braun. A separate entry for February 2026 shows a meeting with Novo Nordisk A/S. A May 2026 entry shows a call with George Yancopoulos of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc.A meeting with the CEO of Tylenol-maker Kenvue Inc. preceded the administration’s White House news conference in which President Donald Trump told pregnant women to avoid the painkiller, citing unproven theories of a link to autism. The meeting occurred three days after the Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration was expected to link the drug to autism.Other entries show meetings with CEOs of infant formula makers, a roundtable with hospital executives and a session with insurance CEOs.Kennedy, who has also criticized the food industry, met in March 2025 with Donnie King, CEO of Tyson Foods Inc. at the time. He has also met with leaders from Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc., Starbucks Corp, and In-N-Out Burgers.Kennedy also met Stacey Kennedy, the US CEO of tobacco company Philip Morris International Inc., the listings show.A June 2026 entry shows a meeting with SoftBank Group Chairman Masayoshi Son along with Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.Kennedy has had regular meetings with Louisiana Senator Bill Cassidy, a key vote for his confirmation.Three CenturiesThe documents appear to range from as early as 1840 (a handwritten catalog of the surgeon general’s library) through the first half of 2026. More than 10,000 records were from previous centuries, according to search results returned by the site.The site is searchable and offers some initial “collections,” prominently featuring a batch of documents on Covid-19. Other collections include records on infant formula, the opioid crisis and several batches related to FOIA litigation.Kennedy’s calendars show meetings with other cabinet officials and media appearances, including briefings on the ongoing measles outbreak starting in February 2025, when cases were increasing in Texas. HHS said it’s also using artificial intelligence to process public records requests and propose redactions for trade secrets or other information subject to withholding. Thousands of documents have been requested under FOIA and the use of AI will allow quicker searches and reviews, the agency said.The transparency website replaces an online reading room that previously aggregated records released under FOIA and other documents.Last year, the Department of Government Efficiency led by Elon Musk cut thousands of staff across HHS, including in the FOIA departments, impairing the agency’s ability to respond to records requests quickly.The Food and Drug Administration has previously published the agency’s response letters for new drug and biologic applications.--With assistance from Ike Swetlitz, Allison DeAngelis, Daniela Sirtori, Redd Brown, Jeff Kao and Ilena Peng.(Updates with additional details starting in fourth paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

items.body:
欧州市場サマリー（24日）
4:47 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

反落して取引を終えた。鉱業や銀行株の売り注文が優勢で、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に下落。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．８４％安だった。

金や銅の値下がりを受けて、資源大手グレンコアは４．８％、アングロ・アメリカンは５．７％、銅大手アントファガスタは８．１％、いずれも下落。

銀行大手のバークレイズは２．５％、ＨＳＢＣは２．７％、スタンダード・チャータードは２．８％、いずれも値下がりした。

一方、日用品のユニリーバは２．０％高。製薬大手ＧＳＫは２．５％、アストラゼネカは２．９％、それぞれ上昇した。

ケータリングサービス大手コンパスは２０２６年９月期決算の売上高が市場予想を上回り、４．２％上昇。オンライン家電販売のＡＯワールドは、需要低迷への懸念から９．３％安。

２５日発表の米個人消費支出（ＰＣＥ）統計の発表に関心が集まる。市場では、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）による１２月に２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げ決定が確実視されている。

ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）は１２月会合で利上げするとの見方が強い。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

反落して取引を終えた。前日大幅上昇したハイテク株が人工知能（ＡＩ）関連や企業統治を巡る懸念から反落し、相場の重荷となった。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種テクノロジー株指数は２．８１％安。

ＵＢＳが投資判断を引き下げたドイツの半導体製造装置メーカー、アイクストロンは１６．３％安。ドイツの半導体大手インフィニオン・テクノロジーズは９．７％、オランダの半導体製造装置メーカーＡＳＭインターナショナルは８．０％、それぞれ下落した。

金や銅の値下がりを受けて、資源株指数は４．６４％安。

一方、ヘルスケア株指数は１．８９％高。フランスの製薬大手サノフィは９．８％上昇。同業の米インスメッドを４１０億ドルで買収すると発表したことが好感された。

食品・飲料株指数は１．１６％、個人・家庭用品株指数は０．８６％、それぞれ上昇した。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　

域内国債利回りが小幅低下した。株式市場が反落し、原油先物価格が約３カ月ぶりの安値圏で推移する中、安全資産への資金流入が幾分下支えとなった。

欧州株と米国株は２３日の大幅上昇から一転、２４日に反落し、一部の資金が債券に向かった。また、北海ブレント先物は、取引序盤に付けた３カ月ぶりの安値から反発、欧州のガス価格も小幅上昇した。

市場はＥＣＢの１２月理事会での利上げをほぼ確実視しており、来年前半に追加利上げが１回実施されるとの見方を織り込んでいる。

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは１ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の３．２７％。

ＥＣＢの政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りは小幅低下の３．０７％。

フランス１０年債利回りは３ｂｐ低下の４．７６％。独仏１０年債利回り格差は１４８ｂｐと、１０月中旬に付けた１７０ｂｐ超の高水準から縮小した。

イタリア１０年債利回りは４．３５％と小幅に上昇した。

FAST

WASHINGTON, Nov 24 : The US Central Intelligence Agency and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence recently discovered a cybersecurity breach that exposed some of their unclassified information, according to a person familiar with the matter.
The intrusions affected a network that looks for intelligence insights in public, unclassified material, according to the New York Times, which first reported on the breach.
While it was not clear specifically what unclassified material was compromised, information at other government agencies was also believed to have been exposed in the breach, the Times added.
Asked about the report, the ODNI said there had been "no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems."
The news is the latest in a series of tech outages and cybersecurity incidents, including a breach reported at the US Department of Agriculture. Two separate breaches have recently been disclosed at the FBI, while the Pentagon and the Department of Homeland Security have also been caught up in recent cyber incidents.
The Times report did not say how the breach occurred.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Bitcoin sell-off driven by weak demand, forced liquidations: 21Shares
items.summary: The $6.4 billion hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance in October triggered Bitcoin’s recent sell-off, but weakening investor demand and forced liquidations drove most of the subsequent losses, ...
items.body:
News
/ Cointelegraph
/ Bitcoin sell-off driven by weak demand, forced liquidations: 21Shares

Bitcoin sell-off driven by weak demand, forced liquidations: 21Shares 2 min read

BTCUSD ETHUSD
The $6.4 billion hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance in October triggered Bitcoin’s recent sell-off, but weakening investor demand and forced liquidations drove most of the subsequent losses, according to a Nov. 24 report from crypto asset manager 21Shares.
While the Oct. 29 hack triggered the initial decline, the report found that weakening demand drove Bitcoin BTCUSD down a further 8.3% between Nov. 4 and Nov. 11. Forced selling of leveraged positions led to the steepest decline, sending BTC down another 13.5% over the next three days. Crypto liquidations totaled $5.8 billion in the week ending Nov. 15, with long positions accounting for 81%.

Bitcoin’s sell-off and leverage unwind. Source: 21Shares
Signs of weakening demand were also seen in the stablecoin supply, which contracted by $10.7 billion following the hack, marking the largest 18-day decline in dollar terms since the Terra collapse in 2022. US spot Bitcoin and Ether ETHUSD exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded combined outflows of $3.9 billion between Oct. 30 and Nov. 13.
Eliezer Ndinga, global head of research at 21Shares, told Cointelegraph that the market was already vulnerable before the hack:
The Fed had raised rates in September, core inflation had risen 0.3% for a third straight month, and doubts over AI spending had kept the Nasdaq-100 below its October 6 record. The hack started the sell-off, but bitcoin fell only 5.1% in the two days after it and had recovered almost all of that by November 4.
The report also found little evidence of selling by other major Bitcoin holders. The 18,270 BTC and 522,409 ETH stolen in the Binance hack remained unspent as of mid-November, while neither the US government nor the Mt. Gox trustee had transferred Bitcoin to exchanges since the attack.
Bitcoin treasury firm Strategy continued buying, adding 2,332 BTC between Oct. 26 and Nov. 15. Meanwhile, miner transfers to exchanges fell to their lowest levels since at least 2020, although the data may not capture sales by publicly traded mining companies.
21Shares sees a K-shaped recovery for crypto
21Shares believes Bitcoin is already more than a year into a cyclical bear market. Historically, such downturns have lasted about two and a half years and resulted in average price declines of 84%, according to the report.
However, the researchers see a low probability of Bitcoin revisiting the depths of previous bear markets, citing the growing presence of institutional investors and spot ETFs. Ndinga said the competitive landscape for crypto has also changed:
Crypto is also no longer the only frontier technology in investors’ minds, with AI and robotics drawing talent and capital away from it. We expect a K-shaped recovery, where bitcoin, 24/7 trading venues, privacy protocols and quantum-resistant solutions advance while other parts of the market lag.
Ndinga warned that a larger-than-expected Federal Reserve rate hike in December could prolong the downturn. Another potential source of selling pressure is the $2.2 billion in BTC and ETH stolen in the Binance hack, which could reach the market through over-the-counter (OTC) brokers in the coming months.
Ndinga identified Bitcoin’s realized price of $53,250, a measure of the average investor cost basis, as a key downside level to watch. Conversely, a return to the $73,000 to $75,500 range coupled with sustained ETF inflows and rising stablecoin balances would signal renewed investor demand.

Stablecoin supply changes following major market shocks. Source: 21Shares

items.body:
スペースＸ、テスラと合併実現ならＳ＆Ｐ５００採用後押し＝ＪＰモルガン
3:49 配信

6月11日作成。 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo（ロイター） [２４日 ロイター] - ＪＰモルガンは２４日、米宇宙企業スペースＸについて、電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラ＜TSLA.O＞との合併が実現すれば、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種への組み入れを後押しする可能性があるとの見方を示した。

英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）によると、米実業家イーロン・マスク氏率いるテスラとスペースＸは、合併交渉を担う２つの特別委員会を主導する取締役として、テスラから３人、スペースＸから２人の計５人を選任した。

スペースＸは現在、Ｓ＆Ｐ５００構成銘柄への採用要件を満たしていない。しかし、過去の事例を踏まえると、テスラとの合併が成立した場合、Ｓ＆Ｐダウ・ジョーンズ委員会が一部要件を免除する可能性があると、ＪＰモルガンのアナリストらは指摘した。

さらに、スペースＸ株のロックアップ（既存株主による売却制限）解除に伴い、Ｓ＆Ｐは浮動株調整ベースでの同社時価総額を見直す見通しで、これによってＳ＆Ｐのより広範な株価指数への組み入れ時期が早まる可能性があるという。

ＪＰモルガンはまた、スペースＸが株価指数に組み入れられれば、浮動株の約１０％に相当するパッシブ運用による買いを誘発する可能性があるとの見方を示した。

items.title: Oil prices fall as supply glut concerns offset West Asia disruption fears
items.summary: Brent crude futures fell 43 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.97 a barrel by 0137 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 47 cents, or 0.6%, to $81.58 a barrel ...
items.body:
Home / Markets / Commodities / Oil prices fall as supply glut concerns offset West Asia disruption fears

Oil prices fall as supply glut concerns offset West Asia disruption fears Brent crude futures fell 43 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.97 a barrel by 0137 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 47 cents, or 0.6%, to $81.58 a barrel

Both benchmarks gained more than 2% on Tuesday | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters TOKYO 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 25 2026 | 8:08 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday, paring some of the previous day's gains, as concerns over supply disruptions in the West Asia were offset by rising supply and the prospect of a market surplus.
Brent crude futures fell 43 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.97 a barrel by 0137 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 47 cents, or 0.6%, to $81.58 a barrel.
Both benchmarks gained more than 2% on Tuesday.
"Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute.
"However, attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and exchanges of attacks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have raised uncertainty over the sustainability of this trend," he said.

Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will be determined at the Opec+ meeting, Ueno added. Opec+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide their 2027 output policy.
The International Energy Agency said on November 13 that the world oil market would return to a surplus in the fourth quarter as West Asia exports recover faster than global oil demand.
Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has reopened after an "unlawful group" closed a valve on the pipeline, with oil beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, the chairperson of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Monday.

Iraq is pressing Opec+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity, four people familiar with the matter said, heightening tensions over a review that will help determine how much members can pump next year.
China and India are on track for record Russian oil imports this year, plugging a supply gap caused by the Iran war, according to tanker data and industry sources.
Meanwhile, a container ship was targeted while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to state media.
On Monday, three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles as they sailed east through the strait, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday.

US crude stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended November 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. 
Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average.

items.body:
Home / World News / Iran slams US over unpaid OPCW dues, warns of threat to global security

Iran slams US over unpaid OPCW dues, warns of threat to global security Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has accused Washington of undermining the OPCW through unpaid dues, warning that the funding crisis could disrupt its operations

Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister | Image Credit: Bloomberg

ANI 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 25 2026 | 7:59 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi on Tuesday criticised the United States for allegedly undermining the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), warning that unpaid US dues are threatening the global watchdog's operations.
In a post on X, Araghchi accused Washington of hypocrisy regarding chemical arms.
"The US is so concerned about chemical arms that it's crippling the world's chemical weapons watchdog," he wrote.
He noted that the OPCW may be forced to suspend work and scale back vital programs, adding that by "obstructing its mandate, the US is deliberately putting global peace and security at risk". Araghchi described the situation as "shameful".
 

Araghchi's remarks accompanied a screenshot of a Reuters report titled, "US arrears leave chemical weapons watchdog facing budget crisis".

Characterising those reports as "pro-Israel media" narratives and "Iraq War-style propaganda," Araghchi flatly rejected the claims as "RUBBISH".

"They talk all the time. All they do is talk, but it's all BS," Trump was quoted as saying by Fox News. "I hope Iranian tankers try to test the blockade. They will all be at the bottom of the sea, like Iran's navy," he said.
The latest remarks come amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with Trump repeatedly expressing dissatisfaction over the terms Iran has been willing to offer in negotiations.

items.body:
Home / World News / Houthis close in on Aden as Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line

Houthis close in on Aden as Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line The Houthis' advance toward Aden has come after forces allied with the government withdrew from areas on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, allowing the Houthis to consolidate their grip on territory

Houthi supporters gather in Yemen’s capital Sana’a as fighting intensifies across several fronts. | Photo: Reuters

AP Dubai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 25 2026 | 7:52 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced to within about 60 kilometres of the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government in the southern city of Aden, but the forces fighting them have set up a fortified line to defend the city, a military official said Tuesday.
Iran reiterated Tuesday that it would not hold talks with the United States to end their conflict unless several conditions are met. It also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite US aerial protection.
Meanwhile, at least nine Palestinians were killed in several Israeli strikes in Gaza, local officials said.
 

Houthi rebels advance toward Aden The Houthis' advance toward Aden has come after forces allied with the government withdrew from areas on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, allowing the Houthis to consolidate their grip on territory around the crucial waterway.
Col. Majed al-Nuzaily, spokesman for the Yemeni army, said the forces that withdrew from the western coast are now stationed north and west of Aden "on a defence line built to stop the Houthi advance," as the rebels come within 60 kilometers of the city.
Also Read

CONFLICT ZONE: Yemen premium

"Aden is a red line. It was a red line in 2015, when the Houthis came to the city and its people drove them out," he said during a virtual briefing.

Speaking in the same briefing, Yemeni foreign ministry official Marwan al-Noman called for the United States and other Western countries to support the Yemeni coast guard in its efforts to intercept smuggled weapons to the Houthis, as well as provide training to Yemeni forces fighting the rebels on the ground.
"The Houthis are a terrorist organisation. They threaten Yemenis first, and then every nation whose ships cross the Red Sea," he said.
Officials say a child is among those killed in Yemen Yemen's Interior Ministry said Tuesday that shelling of areas in Taiz province in southwestern Yemen killed three civilians, including a child, and wounded two other children, citing local police.

The ministry, which is aligned with Yemen's internationally recognised government, blamed the Houthis for the attack.
The Houthis and the Saudi-backed forces in Yemen continue to trade accusations that civilians in their respective territories have been targeted in recent hostilities.

items.summary: DELL shares fell 7.47% to $309.88 in premarket trading at 8:49 a.m. ET on November 24, hours before third-quarter fiscal 2027 results due after the bell. The pullback trims Monday's 20.46% rally to ...
items.body:
News
/ GuruFocus
/ Dell Technologies Stocks Fall 7.47% Hours Before Results Test a $95 Billion AI Backlog

Dell Technologies Stocks Fall 7.47% Hours Before Results Test a $95 Billion AI Backlog Less than 1 min read

DELL
Dell Technologies DELL shares fell 7.47% to $309.88 in premarket trading at 8:49 a.m. ET on November 24, hours before third-quarter fiscal 2027 results due after the bell. The pullback trims Monday's 20.46% rally to $334.91, when AI hardware names surged on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia. Dell's own forecast for the quarter is $49 billion of revenue, plus or minus $500 million, and non-GAAP EPS of $6.50, while the Zacks consensus sits higher at $50.87 billion and $6.76.
The setup rests on one number. In September, Dell reported record second-quarter revenue of $47.0 billion, up 58%, with a record $60.9 billion of AI server orders, $16.4 billion of AI server revenue and a $95 billion backlog. It guided full-year revenue to $192.0 billion and non-GAAP EPS to $25.50, with AI server revenue around $74 billion.

At the premarket price, the shares trade near 12 times that full-year EPS guide, cheap if the backlog converts on schedule at stable margins. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 77/100, a respectable mark held back by middling financial strength and weak momentum after the slide from September highs. The premarket price is about 23% above the GF Value of $252.85, and GuruFocus tags the shares significantly overvalued, a reminder that its model has not caught up with a step change in AI revenue. Watch backlog, AI gross margin and any comment on memory supply tonight.

FAST

Nov 24 : Elon Musk asked a federal appeals court to overturn a jury verdict finding he defrauded Twitter shareholders out of billions of dollars by threatening to abandon his purchase of the social media company four years ago.
In a court filing on Monday night, Musk said shareholders failed to prove that Twitter's stock price fell on May 13, 2022, because he posted that the $44 billion takeover was "temporarily on hold" until Twitter demonstrated that its platform was not overrun by fake and spam accounts.
Musk told the San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals that nothing linked the 9.7 per cent share price decline to $40.72 to any "material falsity" in his post, and that shareholders sought to hold him liable for securities fraud simply because the share price fell.
The world's richest person also said the trial judge should not have certified a class action because many investors likely did not rely on his post when selling Twitter shares.

Lawyers for the shareholders did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Tuesday. One of the lawyers has said Musk might owe $2.6 billion plus interest if the verdict stands.
Class actions let plaintiffs sue as a group, potentially leading to greater damages at lower cost than in individual lawsuits.
Shareholders accused Musk of expressing concern about fake and spam accounts to back out of the takeover or force Twitter to renegotiate a lower price.
They said Twitter's share price remained depressed until Musk agreed in October 2022 to complete his original $54.20 per share offer.
In upholding the verdict in July, US District Judge Charles Breyer in San Francisco found "substantial evidence of falsity" in Musk's May 13 tweet, and said qualms about completing a transaction "do not justify lying to the investing public."
Musk changed Twitter's name to X, and later folded it into his rocket and satellite company SpaceX.

items.author: ロイター

items.summary:
Juveria Tabassum

[２４日 ロイター] - 米家電量販大手ベストバイは２４日、通期の既存店売上高伸び率...
items.body:
ベストバイ、通期売上高見通し上げ　年末商戦の需要に期待
2:22 配信

2025年2月11日に撮影　REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration（ロイター） Juveria Tabassum

[２４日 ロイター] - 米家電量販大手ベストバイは２４日、通期の既存店売上高伸び率見通しを引き上げた。消費者が人工知能（ＡＩ）搭載の新型携帯電話やテレビ、スマートグラスなどのウエアラブル端末に支出する中、年末商戦の堅調な需要を見込む。

通期の既存店売上高伸び率を３．４─４％と予想。従来見通しの１．９─３％から引き上げた。株価は午前の取引で２％超上昇した。

第３・四半期の売上高は５．８％増の１０２億４０００万ドル。ＬＳＥＧがまとめた予想の９９億ドルを上回った。同四半期の調整後１株利益は１．６２ドルと予想を上回った。同社は２７年度の調整後１株利益見通しを６．９０─７．０５ドルに引き上げた。

ジェーソン・ボンフィグ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）によると、テイクツー・インタラクティブの看板ゲームシリーズの待望の新作「グランド・セフト・オートＶＩ」の発売に備える顧客の需要を受け、第３・四半期はゲーム機本体や周辺機器の販売が伸びた。また、「健康管理用リング、ＡＩグラス、トレーディングカードや収集品といった新興カテゴリーが、既存店売上高の伸び率を約１ポイント押し上げている」とした。

幹部は決算説明会で、メモリー半導体のコスト上昇が製品価格を押し上げたものの、パソコン関連の需要は底堅さを維持したと説明した。

同四半期は１５００ドルを超える価格帯の販売が「非常に好調」だった。既存店売上高全体は６．１％増と、予想の２．３％増を大きく上回った。

今月初めにＣＥＯに就任したボンフィグ氏は、燃料費上昇の影響を和らげるため、サプライチェーン内で対応を進めていると述べた。

スティーフルのアナリスト、マイケル・モンタニ氏は、パソコン関連製品と携帯電話がけん引する既存店売上高の伸びは、年末商戦を控えたウォルマート、ターゲット、コストコなど他の小売大手の家電販売にとっても明るい兆候だと指摘した。

items.body:
中国シャオミ7─9月期、自動車市場低迷で57％減益　独への参入計画表明
2:20 配信

写真は中国シャオミのロゴ。2024年4月25日、北京で開催された「北京国際自動車展」で撮影。（ロイター） Ju-min Park

[北京 ２４日 ロイター] - 中国の電気自動車（ＥＶ）・スマートフォンメーカー、小米（シャオミ）が２４日発表した２０２６年第３・四半期（２６年７─９月期）決算は、総売上高が前年同期比５．２％減の１０７２億元、調整後純利益は５７％減の４９億元だった。ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリスト予想平均の５２億元を下回った。中国自動車市場の低迷や部品コストの上昇が響いた。海外展開の強化に向け、２７年後半にドイツの自動車市場に参入する計画も明らかにした。

シャオミの新エネルギー車（ＮＥＶ）、人工知能（ＡＩ）などの新規事業は営業損益が３４億元の赤字。ＮＥＶ事業の売上高は１９．９％減の２２７億元。車両納入台数は７．２％減の１０万９７５台だった。

シャオミは業界データを基に、７─９月期の中国の乗用車市場全体の小売販売は２４％減だったと説明。決算発表後の電話会議で、国内自動車市場の低迷は「全ての企業に大きな圧力」になっていると指摘した。コスト高や在庫増も課題となっているとも強調した。アナリストらは、シャオミの自動車事業は価格競争の激化や中国内自動車市場の低迷にさらされていると指摘している。

スマホの売上高は０．８％減。メモリーの調達コストが高止まりし粗利益率が低下。製品構成を高価格帯のモデルにシフトし、スマホの平均販売価格は前四半期から１０％上昇したという。

シャオミは、ＡＩや自社開発半導体、ロボット分野に関する投資を継続すると説明している。

items.body:
EXCLUSIVE-マイクロソフトが「コードレッド」宣言、大規模障害受け対応見直し
2:14 配信

11月13日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration（ロイター） Jaspreet Singh

[２４日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフトは今月発生した同社サービスの世界的な大規模障害を受け、障害の防止および危機対応体制を全面的に見直す「コードレッド（最も深刻かつ緊急性の高いアラート）」を宣言した。ロイターが入手した社内メモで明らかになった。

マイクロソフトは、今後障害が発生した場合、１時間以内の全世界復旧を目指すことを目標とする。エンジニアがシステムの健全性データをより迅速に診断できるよう、ＡＩエージェントを導入する計画だ。

マイクロソフトを巡っては今月、「チームズ」や「アウトルック」などを含む業務ソフト「マイクロソフト３６５」のサービスが約２４時間にわたり停止。世界の企業や政府機関の業務に大きな影響が及び、エンジニアリングシステムや危機対応体制の不備が露呈した。

Ｍ３６５ Coreのジェイソン・ヘンダーソン社長は２０日、社内メモで、クラウド型メールサービス「エクスチェンジ・オンライン」において、これほど多くの顧客がこれほど長期間にわたりメールを利用できなくなった事例はかつてなかったと指摘。「コードレッドとは、われわれのチームにとって最優先の業務であることを意味する」と説明した。

同社の広報担当者は、問題発生時の迅速な解決だけでなく、将来的なサービス中断を防ぐために可能な限りの措置を講じることにコミットしていると強調。「サービスが復旧したからといって、われわれの仕事が終わったわけではない。各チームは得られた教訓を迅速に反映させ、経営陣はこれを最優先事項として徹底する」と述べた。

items.body:
News
/ Cointelegraph
/ Bitcoin slides amid US tariff nerves as Anthropic falls below IPO price

Bitcoin slides amid US tariff nerves as Anthropic falls below IPO price 2 min read

BTCUSD ANT
Bitcoin struggled to stay above $60,000 at Tuesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks fell on fresh international trade tariff risks.
Key points:
Bitcoin BTCUSD fell below $59,500 on Bitstamp during Tuesday’s US trading session as markets reacted to reports of potential US tariff increases.
Anthropic shares dropped as much as 14% on the day to $75.85, below the company’s $83 offering price.
Economist Robin Brooks said concerns over the Federal Reserve’s policy tightening were contributing to risk-asset downside.
Bitcoin, stocks fall on tariff talk as Anthropic sets new lows
Data from TradingView showed BTCUSD down around 2.2% on the day, having fallen nearly 8% from Monday’s $64,500 high.

BTCUSD 1-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
US equities opened lower, with the S&P 500 down 0.7% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index 2% lower amid reports that the US government is planning to raise tariffs on China and several other economies.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer could announce the results of an investigation into foreign industrial subsidies “as soon as this week.” Partners that signed trade pacts with the US, such as the European Union, Japan and South Korea, could see maximum levies of 15%, the sources said.
Risk assets remain highly sensitive to tariff headlines, having seen snap volatility since President Donald Trump first unveiled sweeping tariffs in April 2025. The US Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed under emergency economic powers in February 2026.
As stocks erased gains seen on the back of Nvidia reinstating CEO Jensen Huang, Anthropic (Nasdaq: ANT) shares fell below their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83. At the time of writing, shares traded near a record low of $75.85, down roughly 14% on the day.

Anthropic shares 15-minute chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
In a Monday analysis, economist Robin Brooks argued that market concerns around further Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes were adding to selling pressure.
“Markets are obviously breathing a sigh of relief in the very short term at Huang’s return to Nvidia, but underlying stress in the system that stems from a Fed wrongly fixated on hikes continues to build,” he said.
Fed officials have upped hawkish language on policy tightening in recent weeks despite inflation prints remaining broadly in line with expectations and oil prices falling to multimonth lows. US WTI crude fell to $79.07 per barrel on Tuesday, a level last seen on Aug. 10.

CFDs on WTI crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The latest data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool continue to show overwhelming market odds of the Fed hiking interest rates by 25 basis points at the Federal Open Market Committee’s (FOMC) Dec. 8-9 meeting.

Fed target-rate probability comparison. Source: CME Group
In a Monday speech at the University of Mount Saint Vincent, New York Fed President John Williams forecast inflation easing to “just above” the central bank’s 2% target next year before hitting that level in 2028.
“We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2 percent goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis. There is still work to do to get that done,” he said.

items.title: フアン氏、エヌビディア社員に謝罪　ＣＥＯ復帰後の買い一服で株価約6％安
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Deborah Mary Sophia　Shashwat Chauhan

[２４日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手エヌビ...
items.body:
フアン氏、エヌビディア社員に謝罪　ＣＥＯ復帰後の買い一服で株価約6％安
1:13 配信

2026年11月23日、ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）。 REUTERS/Brendan McDermid（ロイター） Deborah Mary Sophia　Shashwat Chauhan

[２４日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手エヌビディアの最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）に復帰したジェンスン・フアン氏は２４日、カリフォルニア州サンタクララの本社で開かれた全社員集会で、自身が同社の行動規範の一部に違反し、「いくつかのひどい過ち」を犯したと語った。関係者がロイターに明らかにした。

関係者によると、フアン氏は約１時間にわたる集会で従業員に謝罪するとともに、トランプ大統領がエヌビディア取締役会に圧力をかけて自身の復帰を実現させたというのは事実ではないと述べた。

また、行動規範の一部に違反したことは容認できない行為だったと認め、セラピーを受けていることを明らかにした。

さらに、米紙ニューヨーク・タイムズによると、フアン氏は自身が高圧的な上司だったとする報道に異議を唱えたほか、自らが「法を超越した存在」だから復帰できたとする見方も否定した。

２４日の取引で、エヌビディア株は急落し、約５．９％安で終了。フアン氏のＣＥＯへの電撃復帰を受けた前日の急騰の勢いは早くも失われ、投資家の関心は同社の政治面や企業統治面のリスクに向かった。２３日には３１．５％急騰し、時価総額は９５２０億ドル余り拡大していた。２３日に上昇していた他の人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株も値下がりした。

テロス・ウェルス・アドバイザーズのポートフォリオ運用責任者、ダン・シーハン氏は「復帰そのものが、疑問を解消するのと同じくらい新たな疑問を生んでいる。同氏の復帰で大きな不確実性は取り除かれたが、エヌビディアの企業統治がどう評価されるかという懸念は残る」と指摘。「今後、政府がエヌビディアにどの程度関与するのかという疑問もある。また、復帰という判断が暗に示した姿勢を踏まえると、社内の行動規範をどう管理するかも問われる。株価が急騰しても、こうした問題は解決しない」と語った。

エヌビディアは２３日、トランプ大統領の圧力を受け、不倫問題の発覚で辞任したフアン氏を復帰させた。一連の急展開は市場を揺さぶり、同社の技術や資金に依存するＡＩ関連業界にも動揺が広がった。

米議会では与野党の議員がエヌビディアの決定を厳しく批判し、フアン氏の復帰を巡る経緯を議会が精査すべきだと訴えた。

＜続く調査＞

フアン氏とエヌビディアはともに、米連邦捜査局（ＦＢＩ）、司法省、証券取引委員会（ＳＥＣ）など、州・連邦当局による多数の捜査や審査の対象となっている。

１２月３日には上院の公開公聴会が予定され、フアン氏が証言する見通し。外国の情報機関による活動の可能性や国家安全保障、輸出管理を巡る取締役会独自の調査も続いている。

アンダーセン・キャピタル・マネジメントの創業者、ピーター・アンダーセン氏は「騒ぎが落ち着き始め、人々は（エヌビディアの）決定をより批判的に検討するようになっている。取締役会は自らの決定によって、倫理面と法的な面で極めて大きなリスクを背負った」と述べた。フアン氏による今後の証言も「同社にとって極めて大きなリスク」だと指摘した。

２３日の急騰により、エヌビディアは世界の時価総額ランキングでアップルに次ぐ２位に返り咲いた。ただ、株価はなお１０月６日に付けた過去最高値を約３１％下回っている。

半導体やデータセンター関連銘柄を含むＡＩ関連企業の株価も大幅に上昇し、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種指数の構成銘柄の時価総額は２兆８０００億ドル余り増加した。

テロスのシーハン氏は「２３日の動きは驚きだったが、危機を脱した兆候とは受け止めていない。１つのニュースで時価総額が３兆ドル増える市場は、別のニュースで同じように急落する可能性がある」と述べた。

Exclusive-Microsoft declares 'Code Red' after historic outage, internal memos show

FAST

Nov 24 : Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" drive to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after a 24-hour outage exposed shortcomings in its engineering systems and crisis response, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters.
The November 12-13 outage hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms and disrupted airline communications, fueling broader concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure. Microsoft said the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents.
Microsoft blamed the outage on an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July. CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologized for the disruption.
The Code Red signified the most severe and urgent alert to address weaknesses in Microsoft's engineering and operational practices after the outage disrupted Exchange Online, its cloud-based email service, as well as Outlook, Teams, its Copilot AI assistant and other Microsoft 365 products.

It was the most customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online, M365 Core President Jason Henderson said in a memo to staff on Friday.
Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, he said. "Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team," Henderson added.
'FOG OF WAR'
Amanda Silver, Microsoft's corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, the company's workplace intelligence platform for AI agents, said in a separate memo on Monday that engineers had to work through a "fog of war" as the outage unfolded.
Despite deploying top engineering personnel, responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats and struggled to maintain a cohesive picture of hypotheses and decisions because diagnostic data was scattered across fragmented internal tracking systems, Silver said.
Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced "roughly ten years' worth of acceptable failures," according to Silver's memo.
"Our work doesn't end when service is restored. Our teams keep working around the clock to quickly implement any lessons learned, and our leadership makes sure this is our top priority," a company spokesperson told Reuters when contacted about the memos.
RECOVERY TARGET
As part of the Code Red, a high-priority mobilization reserved for critical crises, Silver outlined five workstreams focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery mechanisms.
Microsoft set a target of achieving worldwide resolution within an hour during future incidents and plans to deploy AI agents to help engineers diagnose system health data more quickly.
Henderson said he would hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team, which oversees the engineering group responsible for underlying Microsoft 365 services, to track actions stemming from the outage, along with weekly reviews.
The company spokesperson said Microsoft is committed not only to resolving issues when they occur, but to doing everything possible to prevent future disruptions.
SLOW PATCH DEPLOYMENTS
"Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday," Henderson said, adding that he had conducted an extensive review of the broader organizational and structural issues that allowed the failures to occur.
In another memo earlier this month reviewed by Reuters, Henderson said "urgent patches to our M365 Core services" took too long to deploy worldwide.
"In a separate recent incident, an urgent production fix took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. For our most urgent security issues, we need to get from detection to safe worldwide deployment in an hour. Needless to say, we aren't here yet," he wrote.

Source: Reuters

US lawmakers raise alarm at FAA decision to deploy aviation AI tool nationally

A view of the control tower at Newark Liberty International Airport in Newark, New Jersey, US, November 14, 2026. REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz

Administrator of the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Bryan Bedford speaks during the "Red, Flight & Blue: The Future of U.S. Aviation," forum at The Hay-Adams hotel, near The White House, in Washington, DC, US, November 18, 2026. REUTERS/Nathan Howard/File Photo

WASHINGTON, Nov 24 : A group of two dozen House Democrats on Tuesday raised serious concerns about the Federal Aviation Administration decision to deploy a new AI tool to assist air traffic controllers nationwide on November 10, days before a major system failure.
The FAA in September began using a new software-based AI tool system in the Washington area that uses predictive analytics to improve how flights are managed after awarding an $875 million, 12-year contract to Air Space Intelligence.
The Democrats, led by Representative Rick Larsen of Washington, the ranking member of the House Transportation Committee, criticized the "sudden expansion of a largely untested system" and asked the FAA to answer a series of questions by November 30. "We have yet to receive any substantive information proving the system was properly validated before its nationwide expansion," the lawmakers wrote.
The system, dubbed Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories, or SMART, uses data to analyze airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, airspace conditions and operational constraints to predict traffic flows and identify potential conflicts before they occur.

The letter cited the nearly five-hour November 13 nationwide ground stop that led flights to be canceled for an estimated 1.5 million passengers due to an FAA telecom issue.
"The federal government is dealing with a crisis of confidence," the letter said. "Americans’ faith in the aviation system is shaken. The opacity and inconsistency with which the FAA has handled the SMART rollout threatens to
further undermine that trust."
The lawmakers want to know the data used by the FAA to validate SMART operations and what redundancies are in place to "ensure reliable ATC operations in the event of issues or outages impacting SMART."
The lawmakers also cited reports that the FAA may have retaliated against employees who raised safety concerns about SMART’s rapid deployment.
The FAA declined comment and said it would respond directly to the lawmakers.
US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has called the tool essentially "dumb AI" and emphasized controllers remain in charge, not the software.
The system uses over 200 data streams, creates data visualizations, and produces scheduling recommendations for operations experts to consider passing along but does not involve active management of planes in the sky.

Source: Reuters

items.body:
ＥＣＢ12月利上げの公算、その後の道筋不透明＝オランダ中銀総裁
0:59 配信

写真はスレイペン・オランダ中銀総裁。3月24日、アムステルダムで撮影。REUTERS/Piroschka van de Wouw（ロイター） [アムステルダム ２４日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行 （ＥＣＢ）理事会メンバーのスレイペン・オランダ中銀総裁は２４日、ＥＣＢは１２月の理事会で利上げに踏み切る公算が大きいが、その後の道筋は不透明であるとの見方を示した。

スレイペン氏はアムステルダムで記者団に対し、「われわれは理事会ごとに判断を下す方法を取っているため、次回１２月の理事会で決定することになる。ただ、方向性は明確だと思う」と述べた。

ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）のナーゲル総裁を含む多くのＥＣＢ政策担当者は、ユーロ圏のインフレ率が高すぎるため、ＥＣＢは来月に金融引き締めを迫られる公算が大きいと述べている。

さらに同氏は、多くの不確実性があり次に何が起こるかを見通すことが難しいため、２０２７年の金融政策の見通しについては言及を避けた。そうした不確実性には、フランスなどの国における債務コストの上昇に関連するリスクも含まれると述べた。

スレイペン氏は、市場の懸念を和らげるため、フランス政府に対し、外部からの支援を期待するのではなく、自ら財政改善に向けた措置を講じるよう促し、「フランスの財政問題は、まずフランス自身で解決する必要がある」と指摘。「大半のエコノミストは、その解決には痛みが伴うと言うだろうが、解決は確実に可能だ」と述べた。

items.title: Copper price erases Nvidia rebound as investors steer clear of metals
items.author: Frik Els
items.creator: Staff Writer
items.summary: Traders have booked up to 100,000 tonnes of US copper for China, a sign they are losing faith in tariffs, BMO Capital Markets says.
items.body:
Copper price erases Nvidia rebound as investors steer clear of metals
Traders have booked up to 100,000 tonnes of US copper for China, a sign they are losing faith in tariffs, BMO Capital Markets says.

Staff Writer
|
November 24, 2026 - 10:53 am

Categories:
Markets

Stock image.

Copper gave back all of Monday’s artificial intelligence-fuelled gains on Tuesday as investors who dumped metals during the recent AI rout showed little appetite to return, and traders kept moving US stockpiles to China.

Comex copper for December delivery fell 3.5% to $5.437 a pound ($11,985 a tonne) in morning trade in New York. A settlement at that level would be the lowest since March 24. The contract settled at $5.634 on Monday, up 2.7% but well off the session high of $5.787 reached after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.

Tuesday’s drop leaves copper 21% below its record settlement of $6.889 on September 9, technically a bear market. The metal is now down 3% this year and 16% in November.

Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was down 3.5% at $12,054 a tonne in official trading after briefly ducking below $12,000, Reuters reports. It had jumped as much as 5.3% on Monday.

Investors who sold commodities during the AI rout that followed Huang’s resignation on November 12 are not rushing back.

“These investors are not fully reengaging the positions they had pre-event, which includes commodity exposure,” Panmure Liberum analyst Tom Price told Reuters. Many have decided copper is too volatile and are cutting commodity exposure to concentrate on AI stocks, he said.

“There are now multiple reasons for the market to short copper,” Aces Zhou, a base metals trader at Hangzhou Chenglian Industrial, told Bloomberg. Beyond the AI narrative, he said, trade flows are starting to reverse as copper leaves the United States, and the factors that supported the metal’s two-year rally are unravelling.

Rate hikes and a strong dollar add to the headwinds. Markets are fully pricing a quarter-point increase at the Federal Reserve’s December meeting, which would be the second this year, Bloomberg reports, and the dollar index is at its highest since March 2025, according to BMO Capital Markets.

US metal heads to China

The physical market remains tight, but financial flows have overpowered it, BMO’s analysts wrote after attending Asia Copper Week in Shanghai last week. Visible exchange inventories cover only about two days of consumption, and the Yangshan premium for imports into China climbed from under $100 a tonne to around $500 in a month.

Those premiums, together with a narrowing gap between New York and London prices, have prompted traders to book an estimated 30,000 to 100,000 tonnes of US cathode for direct shipment to China, BMO said. The metal, held outside exchange warehouses on the US west coast, takes about two weeks to arrive.

The shipments matter less for the tonnage than for what they signal, BMO said: that traders are losing confidence in a tariff decision that would keep US stockpiles sealed off from the rest of the world. Chinese industry players expect President Donald Trump to drop plans for duties on refined copper, while Western participants still lean towards a tariff being imposed.

BMO expects the selloff to extend until Washington signals its tariff intentions or prices fall far enough to hit supply, potentially in the $10,000 to $11,000 a tonne range. Trafigura’s cost curve shows about 10% of copper produced by solvent extraction and electrowinning is already losing money at around $13,000, the bank said. BMO stands by its structurally bullish medium-term view.

Smelters squeezed

Talks on 2027 treatment charges, the fees miners pay smelters to process concentrate, remain far apart. Antofagasta has reportedly offered around minus $200 a tonne, while China’s Tongling has signalled about minus $80 could be acceptable, according to BMO.

This year’s benchmark was set at zero, already a record low, and BMO estimates some Chinese smelters break even on a cash basis at around minus $90. A deeply negative 2027 benchmark could speed up output cuts, especially as falling sulphuric acid prices erode by-product income.

Mine supply remains tight. Global copper mine production fell 1% year on year in September and is down 1% over the first nine months of 2026, the International Copper Study Group said in its latest monthly bulletin. Output from Chile slumped 15% and Peru 9% in the month, more than offsetting gains in Indonesia, China and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Refined demand fell 2% from a year earlier, slightly more than supply, leaving the refined market in deficit for the month, though it remains in surplus for the year to date.

Miners give back gains

Copper stocks reversed much of Monday’s rally. Freeport-McMoRan fell 5% at the New York open, cutting its market value to $68 billion, and Southern Copper lost 4% to $117 billion. Teck Resources dropped 4% to $25 billion, while BHP slipped 2% to $174 billion and Rio Tinto 2% to $125 billion. The five New York-listed heavyweights shed about $15 billion in the first minutes of trading, after adding more than $25 billion on Monday.

In London, Antofagasta dropped 7%, Anglo American almost 6% and Glencore 4%, while Poland’s KGHM fell 7%. In Toronto, First Quantum Minerals lost 6%, Lundin Mining and Hudbay Minerals 5% each and Ivanhoe Mines 4%.

BHP this week outlined plans to spend up to $17.4 billion to roughly double copper output in South Australia to about 650,000 tonnes a year by 2040, with a final investment decision expected in the first half of 2027.

First Quantum Minerals and Panama opened formal negotiations on Monday over the Cobre Panama mine, shut since 2023, after the company accepted the government’s five conditions for talks, including recognition that Panama owns the mineral resource.

Trader Trafigura has taken full control of the $260 million La Farola copper-gold project in Chile, buying the remaining 50% of owner Minera Altair as it moves from trading concentrate into mine development. In Santiago, the price slump is threatening President José Antonio Kast’s budget plans , as copper accounts for about half of the country’s exports.

(With files from Reuters and Bloomberg)

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Medha Singh

[２４日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックが２４日の取引で一時１２％強...
items.body:
アンソロピック一時12％安、公募価格割れ　時価総額2000億ドル減の勢い
0:47 配信

米ニューヨークのタイムズスクエアに掲げられたアンソロピックの看板。11月19日撮影。REUTERS/Shannon Stapleton（ロイター） Medha Singh

[２４日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックが２４日の取引で一時１２％強下落し、新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）価格を下回った。時価総額約２０００億ドルを消失する勢いとなっており、ＡＩ企業の高騰した評価額やコンピューティングインフラに投じられている巨額資金への懸念が強まる可能性がある。

株価は一時１２．６％安の７６．６０ドルと、ＩＰＯ価格の８３ドルを下回った。

アンソロピックは１９日、ナスダック市場に新規上場した。主要ＡＩ開発企業としては世界初の上場で、ＡＩブームの持続性を占う試金石として市場の注目を集めた。初値はＩＰＯ価格を約３４％上回る１１１．５０ドル。その後は１７％高で初日の取引を終えた。ただ、その後はハイテク株全般の売りに押され、下落基調となっている。

２３日は、半導体大手エヌビディアがジェンスン・フアン氏を最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）に復帰させたことが好感され、米株式市場はＡＩ関連株主導で急反発した。しかし、アンソロピックはその上昇相場に乗ることができず、下落して取引を終えた。

ストーンＸのシニアマーケットアナリスト、フィオナ・シンコッタ氏は「データセンター投資の拡大ペースに鈍化が見られれば、アンソロピックの開発スピードに影響を及ぼすことは明らかで、いずれは将来の収益や企業価値にも影響が及ぶだろう」と述べた。

ＩＰＯ後に公募価格を下回ったハイテク関連大手はアンソロピックだけではない。６月に上場した宇宙開発企業スペースＸ は約１カ月後にＩＰＯ価格を下回ったほか、２０１２年にはフェイスブック（現メタ)が上場２日目に公募価格を割り込んだ。

ただ、指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩは１１月３０日の取引終了後、アンソロピック株をグローバル・スタンダード指数に組み入れる予定で、株価の支援材料となる可能性がある。

items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang said he violated code of conduct, source says
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Addressing staff at a meeting at Nvidia's headquarters in California, CEO Jensen Huang said it was untrue that he was reinstated because of pressure from US President Donald Trump on the board.

Nvidia's Jensen Huang said he violated code of conduct, source says

Addressing staff at a meeting at Nvidia's headquarters in California, CEO Jensen Huang said it was untrue that he was reinstated because of pressure from US President Donald Trump on the board. 

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks at Dreamforce 2026 summit in San Francisco on Sep 15, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Carlos Barria)

FAST

Nvidia's reinstated CEO Jensen Huang told employees on Tuesday (Nov 24) that he had violated some of the company's code of conduct and made "some terrible mistakes", one person familiar with the matter told Reuters.
Addressing staff at an hour-long all-hands meeting at Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara, California - a day after he returned as head of the company he co-founded three decades ago - Huang said it was untrue that he had been reinstated because of pressure from US President Donald Trump on the board, the person said.
Huang said he was in therapy and acknowledged it was not acceptable to have violated aspects of Nvidia's code of conduct, the person said.
Nvidia's shares closed 5.9 per cent lower as the historic rally sparked on Monday by Huang's reinstatement lost steam, with investors refocusing on the political and governance risks surrounding his return.

His resignation last week over revelations of extramarital affairs , one with an alleged Chinese spy, roiled markets and unsettled the AI ecosystem reliant on the chipmaker's technology and funding. Trump took credit forbringing back Huang.
Huang apologised while disagreeing with reports that he had been an abusive boss, the New York Times reported, citing a livestream of the meeting it had reviewed.
Huang also rejected claims that he returned because he was a "tech bro" and "above the law", and said he returned because Nvidia's board had evaluated facts and was assured that there was no threat to national security, NYT and Bloomberg News reported.
Nvidia said in a statement on Monday that based on US government input, the board was confident that "Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk", a claim backed by Trump in an interview with CNBC.

Related:

Commentary: Jensen Huang should never have been too big to fail at Nvidia

Jensen Huang’s stunning return as Nvidia CEO: A timeline of events

US lawmakers from both parties sharply criticised Nvidia's decision, saying Congress should scrutinise the circumstances surrounding Huang's return.
"The reinstatement itself raises as many questions as it answers. His return removes a major uncertainty, but what it leaves behind is an overhang on how Nvidia's governance is viewed," said Dan Sheehan, director of portfolio management at Telos Wealth Advisors.
"There are also questions ... about how involved the government will be in Nvidia, and about governance of conduct internally given the stance the reinstatement implicitly took. Those don't get resolved by a soaring stock price."
In an interview with the New York Post, Trump said that he's willing to pardon Huang if necessary but that he believes the reinstalled Nvidia CEO should be fine without one.
Trump also told the New York Post that Nvidia's success was essential to the US retaining an edge in AI and that he's even open to the company giving the American government an equity stake, noting Intel handed more than 10 per cent of its stake last year.
"I thought about it. I said, 'You know, maybe I should do it,' but I didn't bring it up at this point. It's probably not too late," Trump told the New York Post.

Related:

Jensen Huang is back, but questions facing Nvidia remain, say analysts 

Nvidia board's Huang reversal raises doubts about independence, critics say

Nvidia and the White House could not immediately be reached for comment outside regular business hours.
UNDER THE SCANNER Both Huang and Nvidia are facing a host of state and federal probes and reviews, including from the FBI, the Justice Department and the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
A public Senate hearing is set for Dec 3, where Huang is due to testify, while the board's own investigations into potential foreign intelligence efforts, national security and export controls are still underway.
"Now that the dust is beginning to settle, people are taking a more critical look at (Nvidia's) decision ... They (board) put themselves at a tremendous ethical and legal risk by the decision they made," said Peter Andersen, founder of Andersen Capital Management.
Huang's upcoming testimony is also an "enormous risk to the company", he said.
The surge on Monday propelled Nvidia back into second place among the world's most valuable companies, behind Apple, although the stock remains almost 31 per cent below its Oct 6 record high.
AI-related companies, including chipmakers and data-center stocks, rose sharply as well, while the benchmark S&P 500 added more than US$2.8 trillion in market value.
"As incredible as Monday was, I don't take it as a sign we're out of the woods ... a market that can rise US$3 trillion on one headline can fall just as fast on another," Telos' Sheehan said.

Source: Reuters/lk

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 24 : The dollar slipped on Tuesday, giving back much of Monday's gains, as a sharp rally in AI stocks sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO faded, and traders questioned whether the greenback had climbed too far, too fast.
The US currency has been supported by bets that the Federal Reserve will keep raising interest rates, since growth remains strong and inflation is still stubbornly above the Fed's 2 per cent target.
Still, "the US growth edge over the euro zone, UK, and Japan narrowed further in November," which could weigh on the dollar, said Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman.
Fed funds futures traders are pricing in 97 per cent odds of a Fed hike in December, and a 66 per cent chance of an additional increase in January, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool.

Huang's reinstatement on Monday gave equities some relief, but some analysts are questioning how long it will last. 
Recent stock market wobbles have raised questions about how far the Fed can tighten without hurting the economy. The AI trade has lifted the dollar by drawing capital into the US and raising growth expectations. The dollar also tends to act as a safe haven when stocks fall.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.47 per cent to 103.81, with the euro up 0.6 per cent at $1.0966.
US data on Tuesday showed that consumer confidence increased more than expected in November, touching its highest level in nearly two years, amid optimism over labor market conditions and the overall economy following this month's midterm elections. 
The single currency was also boosted by data showing that German business morale rose for a seventh straight month in November.
The Japanese yen weakened 0.16 per cent against the greenback to 159.24 per dollar. Sterling strengthened 0.64 per cent to $1.3112.
The Australian dollar  gained 0.24 per cent to $0.6641, but remained near 11-month lows. In the last month, it has been the worst-performing major currency against the dollar, with a drop of more than 5 per cent as traders price in the prospect of rate cuts.
Analysts at JPMorgan said short positions in the Aussie dollar have "accumulated substantially," with bearish positioning reaching "extreme levels in some cases" by their metrics.
Weekly data from the US markets regulator shows speculators hold their largest bearish position in the Aussie on record, worth some $12.25 billion, according to LSEG calculations.
"Looking first at options, AUD puts have been outnumbering calls for several months now. Early in this process, it seemed reasonable to assume that this might simply be macro hedging, rather than actual outright directional positioning. But the flows have probably migrated to the latter of late," JPMorgan said. 
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 2.40 per cent to $59,824. 
(Additional reporting by Amanda Cooper and Rae Wee, editing by Deepa Babington and Cynthia Osterman)

Source: Reuters

(Fixes dropped numeral in second bullet point, 13.1 billion rather than 3.1 billion)
By Will Dunham
WASHINGTON, Nov 24 : A quasar, one of the universe's most energetic and luminous objects, is the enormously bright core of a galaxy, powered by a central supermassive black hole. Astronomers have now found the oldest-known quasar, one that formed so early in cosmic history that they are still trying to decipher how it happened.
They identified a quasar dating to more than 13.1 billion years ago when the cosmos was less than 5 per cent of its current age, some 630 million years after the Big Bang event that initiated the universe. The quasar dates to 40 million years earlier than the previous record holder, disclosed in July.

"I think it adds to the evidence that some objects in the early universe developed remarkably quickly. Just 630 million years after the Big Bang, this black hole had already grown to about 360 million times the mass of the sun and was shining as a quasar," said astronomer Julien Wolf of the European Southern Observatory in Germany, lead author of the research published in the journal Astronomy and Astrophysics.
Black holes are extraordinarily dense objects with gravity so strong that not even light can escape.
The quasar was first detected by the European Space Agency's Euclid orbiting telescope and then further characterized using a combination of ground- and space-based telescopes. 
The researchers gave the quasar the nickname Dún Aonghasa, the name of an ancient stone fort in Ireland that is perched atop a cliff overlooking the vast expanse of the Atlantic Ocean.
A supermassive black hole that powers a quasar is typically billions of times more massive than the sun. 
"As enormous amounts of gas, dust and matter fall toward the black hole, they form a swirling accretion disk that heats up to extreme temperatures and radiates tremendous amounts of energy, outshining the entire rest of the galaxy by factors of hundreds or even thousands," said astronomer and study co-author Silvia Belladitta of the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy in Germany and the INAF Bologna Observatory of Astrophysics and Space Science in Italy.
"This makes quasars visible across billions of light-years, allowing us to observe them from the very early universe. Studying quasars helps astronomers understand how the first galaxies formed and evolved, and how the supermassive black holes at their hearts grew to such enormous sizes," Belladitta said.
The Dún Aonghasa supermassive black hole is about 90 times more massive than the one at the center of our Milky Way.
A TRANSFORMATIVE EPOCH
It dates to one of the universe's most dramatic and transformative epochs. After the Big Bang, the cosmos cooled into a dark and neutral fog of hydrogen gas. The first stars and galaxies then began to ignite, and their intense radiation slowly burned through the fog, making the universe transparent to light for the first time.
"This process was still unfolding at the time this quasar and its host galaxy were forming. It is a remarkable epoch to find such an object. The supermassive black hole powering this quasar had already grown to an enormous mass in an extremely short time, which challenges our understanding of how black holes can grow so large so quickly in the early universe," Belladitta said.
One possibility is that this black hole started out small after the demise of a star that was part of the first stellar generation, but the observations indicated it was consuming material at a rate too slow to have achieved its great mass so quickly. Another possibility is that it may have been born big in a formation scenario called direct collapse. 
"Normally, a large cloud of gas cools and breaks up into smaller clumps that form stars. Under the right conditions, the gas could stay warm enough to limit that fragmentation, allowing much of it to flow towards the center. That gas can build up a single enormous star that quickly collapses into a black hole. That black hole would start out far more massive than the remnant of a typical first-generation star," Wolf said.
The researchers said Euclid may yet spot quasars at farther distances — meaning older — than Dún Aonghasa, with theoretical models suggesting that the first quasars could potentially date to 270 million to 470 million years post-Big Bang.
"So in short: this is the furthest quasar we have ever seen, but maybe not the furthest there is to find," Belladitta said.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982
items.summary: Key takeawaysThe Bitcoin price fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday, cutting short a recovery that had taken the cryptocurrency above $64,000 a day earlier. But perhaps the more troubling development ...
items.body:
News
/ NewsBTC
/ Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982

Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982 4 min read

BTCUSD XAUUSD
Key takeaways
Bitcoin fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday after a Monday recovery above $64,000, while gold is in its own severe correction.
Gold fell 24.6% over the 60 days to November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982.
Neither asset pays income while interest-bearing investments look more attractive, and selling gold does not automatically send money into Bitcoin.
The October PCE report on November 25 is the next test: the previous reading showed headline inflation of 3.6% and core inflation of 3.1%.
The Bitcoin price fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday, cutting short a recovery that had taken the cryptocurrency above $64,000 a day earlier. But perhaps the more troubling development for investors is happening outside the crypto market.
Gold is going through a severe correction of its own, leaving investors in two assets often associated with wealth preservation facing substantial losses.
This is not the first time Bitcoin and gold have struggled simultaneously. What makes the current environment particularly difficult is that neither asset generates income at a time when interest-bearing investments offer an increasingly attractive alternative.
The question is no longer simply whether Bitcoin is digital gold. It is whether investors have enough reason to own either asset under current monetary conditions.
Gold’s Selloff Exposes A Bigger Problem For Bitcoin
The selling extended well beyond Bitcoin. Figures from the World Gold Council show that Bitcoin lost 13.7%, gold fell 8.3% and the Nasdaq dropped 10%, while the US Dollar Index gained 0.4%. The numbers point to a broader reduction in risk exposure rather than a selloff specific to crypto.

Weekly performance through November 20, 2026. Source: Bloomberg / World Gold Council, Weekly Markets Monitor, November 23, 2026.
Gold declined 24.6% over the 60 days ending November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982.
The World Gold Council’s latest market assessment, published on Monday, identified several risks facing the precious metal, including pressure on leveraged equity and credit positions, restrictive monetary policy and the possibility of another disappointing US inflation report.
The organization also identified the lack of a clear reduction in speculative positioning as a concern.
This matters for Bitcoin because the argument for buying BTC during a gold correction often assumes that capital leaving one scarce asset will eventually find its way into the other.
There is little reason to assume that happens automatically.
An investor selling gold to reduce leverage or meet a margin requirement is unlikely to replace that exposure immediately with Bitcoin. The priority is raising cash, not finding another store of value.
There is also a difference between selling an asset because its investment thesis has deteriorated and selling because the cost of maintaining a position has become too expensive. The latter can create opportunities for patient buyers, but it rarely provides a reliable indication of when a market will bottom.
Bitcoin’s Recovery Is Still Missing Conviction
Monday’s trading session offered Bitcoin investors some encouragement. The cryptocurrency recovered above $64,000 following the previous week’s decline to its lowest levels in roughly two years.
The move did not hold.

Bitcoin (BTC) price, September 1 to November 21. Source: Coinglass.
The broader picture is hardly encouraging. Bitcoin has lost nearly 24% over the past three months, falling from a period high of $86,578 to a low of $58,178. Although BTC has since recovered above $60,000, the bounce has done little to change the broader downward trend.
Tuesday’s return below $60,000 raises questions about the strength of the recovery, particularly given the improvement in technology stocks during Monday’s session.
If Bitcoin struggles to sustain gains when conditions improve elsewhere, investors should be careful about assuming that another equity market rally will necessarily pull BTC higher.
There is also an important distinction between a recovery driven by fresh buyers and one driven by traders closing profitable short positions. Both can produce impressive green candles. Only the former demonstrates that investors are willing to commit new capital at higher prices.
Spot trading activity, ETF subscriptions and derivatives positioning will offer a better indication of which type of recovery the market is experiencing.
For now, the failure to retain Monday’s gains makes the rebound less convincing than its initial size suggested.
Does This Undermine Bitcoin’s Digital Gold Thesis?
Bitcoin’s recent performance will inevitably revive criticism of its role as a store of value. However, gold’s own losses make that argument considerably less straightforward.
The metal has been used to preserve wealth for centuries, yet it remains vulnerable to changes in interest rates, investor positioning and the strength of the US dollar.
Bitcoin shares some of those vulnerabilities while carrying considerably different market risks, including its dependence on speculative demand and the availability of leverage across cryptocurrency exchanges.
That does not invalidate Bitcoin’s scarcity argument. Its supply characteristics have not changed because its market price has fallen.
What the current correction does challenge is the assumption that scarcity alone guarantees protection during financial stress.
An asset can have a credible long-term investment case and still be a poor short-term hedge. Bitcoin investors would benefit from separating those two propositions rather than defending both every time the market declines.
The Next Test Comes From The Federal Reserve’s Preferred Inflation Measure
The immediate focus now turns to Wednesday’s US inflation release.
The Bureau of Economic Analysis is scheduled to publish its October personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report on November 25. The previous release showed annual headline PCE inflation of 3.6%, with core inflation at 3.1%.

US personal income and outlays data. Source: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA).
Another stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce expectations of restrictive monetary policy, making conditions more difficult for assets that rely heavily on capital appreciation.
A softer reading, particularly if accompanied by falling Treasury yields, could offer some relief to both Bitcoin and gold.
For Bitcoin, however, recovering $60,000 should be treated as a starting point rather than confirmation of a broader reversal. Monday’s trading high above $64,000 represents a more demanding test of whether buyers are prepared to return.
Until that happens, the market has demonstrated that it can bounce. It has yet to demonstrate that it can sustain a recovery.

LONDON, Nov 24 : The BBC will make a selection of its CBeebies children's programmes available on Netflix in Britain from December 2, as the publicly funded broadcaster explores new ways of reaching audiences through commercial streaming platforms.
• The limited trial will feature a CBeebies-branded hub on Netflix, offering a selection of programmes such as "Hey Duggee" and "Teletubbies", the BBC said
• The British broadcaster, which is funded by a licence fee paid by TV-watching households, said iPlayer, its own streaming platform, would remain the home of the full CBeebies experience
• Netflix has committed to funding a small number of new CBeebies commissions, the BBC said

FAST

Nov 24 : Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell about 16 per cent on Tuesday as investors focused on the company's shrinking margins amid soaring costs, even as strong AI demand boosted its full-year revenue outlook.
The stock has more than doubled this year through Monday's close, but is set to lose about $10 billion in market value if current losses hold. On Monday, HPE soared more than 17 per cent as an Nvidia-fueled rally lifted AI stocks.
HPE forecast adjusted operating margin for the fiscal year ending October 2027 between 14 per cent and 15 per cent, from 15.1 per cent in fiscal 2026. At its Cloud and AI unit, which includes servers and storage and is a key growth driver, HPE expects annual fiscal margin of about 14 per cent, down from 15.2 per cent in the previous fiscal.
HPE finance chief Marie Myers said on an earnings call that costs were rising faster than pricing and margins would take a hit in the second half of the year as the company ships more AI servers.

"When input costs go up and you don't pass enough of that along, you have to hit your margins and that clearly showed," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B Riley Wealth.
"That raises concerns that the pricing tailwinds are beginning to fade. With supply shortages expected through 2028, that will take a bite out of margins," he added.
However, robust demand for AI servers demand helped drive a 50 per cent jump in HPE's fourth-quarter revenue to $14.55 billion, topping estimates. The company now expects fiscal 2027 revenue growth between 27 per cent and 35 per cent, up from its earlier forecast of 13 per cent to 17 per cent.
"The market seems to be acutely sensitive to any potential changes in profit margins when it comes to tech companies these days," said Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research.
"HPE's solid numbers and robust forecast certainly don't seem to justify today's market's reaction."

Nov 24 : Spotify was back online on Tuesday after the music streaming service was down briefly for thousands of US users earlier in the day, according to outage tracking website Downdetector.com.
User reports peaked at more than 14,000 at around 6:45 a.m. ET, according to Downdetector, which tracks outages by collating status reports from a number of sources. Reports had fallen sharply to about 600 as of 7:17 a.m. ET.
Downdetector's numbers are based on user-submitted reports. The actual number of affected users may vary.
Spotify said on X it was aware of "some issues" and was looking into it, and later added, "Everything's looking much better now."

Nov 24 : Best Buy raised its annual comparable sales growth target on Tuesday, betting on robust demand during the holiday shopping season as customers spend on new AI-enabled phones and TVs as well as wearable technology such as smart glasses.
"We're seeing the emerging categories bucket ... health rings, AI glasses, and trading cards and collectibles are driving about a full point of comp (comparable sales growth) for us," CEO Jason Bonfig told Reuters.
Affluent consumers have been splurging on pricier nice-to-have products across categories from dual-screen phones to Coach handbags, as they lock in gains from stock market portfolios and investments in assets such as real estate.
In contrast, lower- and middle-income consumers have sharply pulled back spending, with inflation and high gas prices crimping budgets, exacerbating a K-shaped effect among US consumers this year.

Consumers have also been upgrading their phones, laptops and other gadgets for AI-enabled options, often at higher price points, driving an upgrade cycle for the electronics retailer.
Best Buy said it saw "significant strength" in its business above the $1,500 price point in the three months through October, when total comparable sales jumped 6.1 per cent and handily beat estimates of 2.3 per cent growth.
The company was working within its supply chain to dull the hit from higher fuel costs, said Bonfig, who took over as CEO earlier this month.
Retailers across the board have warned of higher freight costs this year as the US war on Iran drags up oil prices.
Best Buy now expects annual comparable sales to rise between 3.4 per cent and 4 per cent, compared with its earlier target of 1.9 per cent to 3 per cent growth. Its stock rose about 2 per cent in morning trading.
Comparable sales growth driven by computing and phones is a positive sign for electronics at Walmart, Target and Costco heading into the holiday shopping season, said Stifel analyst Michael Montani.
Higher memory chip costs have driven up product prices, but computing demand remained resilient, Best Buy executives said on a post-earnings call.
Trade-ins on older products, credit card financing options and some promotions were levers Best Buy was pulling to support sales in the category, executives added.
Best Buy's total revenue rose 5.8 per cent to $10.24 billion in the third quarter, beating estimates of $9.90 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.
As customers prepared for the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI", the much-awaited installment in Take-Two Interactive's flagship franchise, Best Buy saw growth in gaming hardware and accessories in the third quarter, Bonfig said.
The company raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings per share target to between $6.90 and $7.05, after quarterly adjusted earnings of $1.62 per share topped estimates.

items.title: Why House Democrats Are Embracing Medicare for More
items.author: Ronald Brownstein
items.creator: Ronald Brownstein

AI boom looms over Warsh's Fed as inflation worries grow

FILE PHOTO: US Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks at a press conference, following a two-day meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), at the Federal Reserve in Washington, DC, US, October 28, 2026. REUTERS/Kylie Cooper/File Photo

FAST

WASHINGTON, Nov 24 : Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has called artificial intelligence a "hinge" of history critical to US leadership, but the technology has also become key to Fed policy as officials debate whether the AI boom is a transformational moment, a source of inflation, or the harbinger of an economic meltdown. 
For Warsh, who calls himself "cautiously optimistic" about what he refers to as "super intelligence," as President Donald Trump does, it may be an all-of-the-above dilemma that challenges the US central bank and his leadership of it.
"This is a serious test for Warsh," Evercore ISI Vice Chairman Krishna Guha, a former New York Fed official, wrote after major US equity indexes closed last week in correction territory. They were dragged down by nervousness about AI's ability to pay off and by unease over the scandal around AI chip giant Nvidia and the brief ouster of its CEO.
Recent inflation and growth data "is too hot and too strong ... But with growth dependent on AI investment and AI consumer net-worth effects, the Fed needs any weakening to remain contained," Guha wrote. "Warsh needs to balance the data with markets that suggest the forward look is cooler, and his desire to assert inflation credibility with his desire not to go down in history as the Fed chair who blew up the AI boom."
